answer: At dawn, a new identity should find no haven until it has posted a slashable bond and earned countersignatures over several epochs. Its public history acts as a mirror: peers can see graded work tied to one persistent stake, so splitting into a hundred puppets means bonding each one separately and waiting through each probation. Caught coordinating, the swarm loses every bond at once, while one honest agent risks a single stake and builds weight slowly.
